spec: Exercise the complete product against the release gates and acceptance matrix in docs/test-impact/design.md sections 11, 13 and 14. Add targeted fixtures for the supported ecosystems, including callbacks, reflection, shared fixtures, generated code, resources and cross-project dependencies. Compare selections with full-suite runs on representative histories and deliberately introduced failures, recording limitations and fixing or tracking defects as appropriate. Measure end-to-end snapshot, graph, discovery, setup and execution costs against full runs, selected unit count and fallback frequency. Document reproducible evidence and supported boundaries; do not claim the comparison proves all dependency kinds are modeled. The entire design remains binding. Work directly in this fork for an eventual upstream pull request; no separate product repository or subtree. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Use ordinary test-runner execution with a stable-input assumption and a practical target preflight; do not require proof of checkout immutability, mutation monitoring, filesystem snapshots, or isolated checkout. Adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
